exposure: personalized obstetric care (health education and psychological intervention)
cohort: The study included 72 women with pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) who were randomly divided into an experimental and a control group.
finding: Personalized obstetric nursing care significantly reduced the incidence of eclampsia and preeclampsia, lowered blood pressure, and improved maternal satisfaction, neonatal Apgar score, and neonatal weight compared to conventional care.
mod_finding: The natural delivery rate was significantly higher in the experimental group receiving personalized obstetric care.
birth_weight: Neonatal weight was measured as an outcome, but specific inclusion criteria for birth weight are not mentioned.
